forms:
You can use moves by pressing <$keyicon(1)>. Using a move reduces
your <$cdef(27)>PP. Your current <$cdef(27)>PP is shown as a gauge at the bottom
right of the screen.

There are many different kinds of moves. Try each one out and
change the terrain to restore homes for all the Pokémon!

Press <$keyicon(3)> to <$cdef(27)>jump. This will allow you to get over holes and other
obstacles with a little bit of air time!

Select an item in your bag, then press <$keyicon(66)> to hold it in your
hands. If you talk to a Pokémon while holding an item, you can
choose to <$cdef(27)>give it to them as a present!

You can become closer friends with Pokémon by talking to them,
giving them presents, and helping them with their <$cdef(27)>requests.
Pokémon who really like you may also give you presents, so try to
make friends with lots of different Pokémon!

You can use this move to make tall grass grow. It won’t work in
certain areas.

Eat <$cdef(27)>salad to power up <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(1)>. You can then press and hold
<$keyicon(1)> to grow tall grass over a larger area.

When powered up, <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(1)> can grow moss or vines on rocks,
walls, and other surfaces.

Place a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1440)> on a house to make it your home.
For block houses, you can place the flag nearby. You can also
invite other Pokémon to live with you.

Place a variety of furniture in your home to increase your
<$cdef(27)>comfort level.

You can create a <$cdef(27)>block house by enclosing a space within four
walls and a door. Just like with a <$cdef(27)><$bname(12)>, Pokémon will move in
if you place three different pieces of furniture inside.

A <$cdef(27)>block house can be made without a <$cdef(27)>building kit as long as you
place the blocks correctly. However, it can’t be destroyed with
a <$cdef(27)>demolition kit or moved with a <$cdef(27)>relocation kit.

At a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(764)>, you can use materials to craft items from
<$cdef(27)>recipes you’ve learned. You can find new <$cdef(27)>recipes around the
world—or, in certain situations, come up with your own.

You can make a Pokémon more <$cdef(27)>comfortable by clearing a path
from their home to a <$cdef(27)>Pokémon Center. If a Pokémon seems to be
having trouble going for a walk, try tidying up the paths around
their home!

You can use this move to break dirt, rock, and other materials
with your fist. This will let you punch holes in walls or the ground.

Press and hold <$keyicon(1)> to continuously use <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(4)>. You can
look up or down while using this move to redirect your smash.

Eat <$cdef(27)>hamburger steak to power up <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(4)>. When powered
up, <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(4)><$cdef(27)> can break harder substances than usual.

If you manage to take a photo of a Pokémon during a photo op,
it will be added to your <$cdef(27)>highlight reel.

If you manage to snag a photo for your highlight reel, you may
receive fabulous rewards, such as photo frames! Keep adding to
your highlight reel by not missing out on photo ops!

Use this move to till dirt or grass into crop fields. Once you’ve
made a crop field, you can plant vegetable seeds in it. You can’t
till dry dirt—use moves like <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(3)> to make the ground
nice and moist for tilling.

You can use <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(2)> on plants and flowers to pick them up.
Plants picked up this way can be given to other Pokémon as
presents or stored in your bag!

Once a day, you can use the <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1444)> inside to fully
restore your <$cdef(27)>PP.

Sometimes a Pokémon with the <$icon(11001)><$cdef(27)>trade specialty will trade items
with you at the <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1325)> inside the <$cdef(27)>Pokémon Center.

If there are places up high that you can’t reach by jumping, you
can place blocks of material, such as dirt or sand, and climb them
like a set of steps.

You can use <$cdef(27)>Stockpile to swallow items that are too big to carry in
your hands, such as furniture, and store them in your bag.

You can use <$cdef(27)>Spit Out to place the items you’ve stockpiled in your
bag. Just go where you want to place an item, then press <$keyicon(0)> to
spit it out.

You can adjust the height at which you place an item by changing
where the camera is facing. This can come in handy when placing
wall-hanging items up high or filling holes in the ground.

You can adjust where you place an object by moving the camera
as you’re placing it. If you point the camera straight down, you
can place objects under your feet to lift yourself up one block at
a time.

If you make paths nicer, such as by smoothing over cracked
ground or placing steps on hills, you can encourage Pokémon to
travel farther from their homes.

When Pokémon go for a walk, they can visit buildings, such
as <$cdef(27)>Pokémon Centers or other Pokémon’s homes.

You can store your items inside a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(2045)>. If your bag gets
full, make some space by putting items in here!

You can also press and hold <$keyicon(196)>, then press <$keyicon(67)> to <$cdef(27)>transfer half
a stack of items.

If you place a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(2045)> next to a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(764)>, you can
use materials directly from the box when crafting items!

You can use this move to cut what’s in front of you, such as trees
or wooden objects, with sharp blades.

Eat <$cdef(27)>bread to power up <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(5)>. You can then press and hold <$keyicon(1)>
to slice up things that are farther away.

When powered up, <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(5)> can slice up harder substances
than usual.

As a <$cdef(27)>Ditto, you can make yourself smaller to fit through tight
spaces. You’ll return to your normal size once you’re back out in
the open.

Tilt <$keyicon(194)> slightly to walk in that direction. If you tilt it all the way,
you’ll start running. If you press and hold <$keyicon(55)> or press <$keyicon(54)>, you
can run even faster.
Tilt <$keyicon(195)> to move the camera.

You can use this move to spray water and revitalize dried dirt and
withered plants, such as grass, trees, and flowers.

Eat <$cdef(27)>soup to power up <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(3)>. You can then press and hold
<$keyicon(1)> to spray water over a larger area.

Items you obtain are placed in your bag. Press <$keyicon(159)> to access your
bag. From there, you can use any items you have.

There’s a limit to how many items you can fit in your bag. You can
increase this limit by purchasing <$cdef(27)>Packing Tips from the <$cdef(27)>shop.

Grass, trees, rocks, furniture, and other items can be placed near
each other in certain combinations to create Pokémon habitats.
Placing the same combination of items in a different location—
such as near water or in a high place—might even create a
different habitat altogether!

When you create a new habitat, a Pokémon you haven’t yet
registered in your <$cdef(27)>Pokédex may appear there. Try making all sorts
of habitats to meet a wide variety of Pokémon friends!

If you’ve learned multiple moves, press <$keyicon(142)> or <$keyicon(143)> to switch
between them. You can register moves by holding <$keyicon(142)> or <$keyicon(143)>,
or by pressing and holding <$keyicon(246)>.

Sometimes you may notice something sparkling on the ground.
You can investigate these sparkling areas to discover traces of
a Pokémon, which will provide information about that Pokémon’s
habitat and preferred environment. This information will be
recorded in your <$cdef(27)>Pokédex.

You can learn about <$cdef(27)>Pokémon and their habitats by investigating
traces. The info you gather is recorded in your <$cdef(27)>Pokédex.

If you walk toward a block, you can climb on top of it.
However, you can’t climb on top of anything that’s more
than one block high.

Follow these steps to <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(1)> a house.
1. Place a <$cdef(27)>building kit in the spot where you wish to build.
2. Collect the materials listed in the kit.
3. Gather Pokémon who meet the requirements of the kit.
It will take a little time for the building process to complete.

Talk to a Pokémon who meets the requirements of the <$cdef(27)>building kit
you placed and have them follow you to it. Once there, you can
ask them to help with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(1)>ing process!

You can use a different <$cdef(27)>building kit to <$cdef(27)>remodel an existing house
or <$cdef(27)>Pokémon Center into a whole new house with all of the same
furniture inside. However, you cannot turn a large house into a
smaller one.

A newly built house does not come with any furniture. Pokémon
cannot live in a house until it has three different pieces of
furniture inside.

If you talk to a Pokémon who is following you while you’re both
near a house, you can invite them to live in that house. Pokémon
are <$cdef(27)>very comfortable in houses and love living in them!

When powered by electricity, certain houses will light up and the
machines inside will start running. Try placing <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1396)> to
provide power to a house.

You can take pictures of Pokémon and other things around you
using your camera. Enter photo mode by pressing <$keyicon(52)> or selecting
<$cdef(27)>Camera in the <$keyicon(4)> menu. Once in photo mode, press <$keyicon(155)> to take
a picture!

Press <$keyicon(49)> while in photo mode to change the way you hold
the camera.

Once you get the <$cdef(27)><$ifull(4000)>, you’ll be able to fix your
camera on the tripod and move freely while you take photos.
Press <$keyicon(49)> while in selfie mode to fix the camera in place.

You may sometimes find <$cdef(27)>lost relics buried in the ground.
Try showing them to a Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(25)> specialty!

Some items you find buried in the ground are unstable and could
explode at any minute! If you happen upon one of these, quickly
spray it with water!

Press and hold <$keyicon(153)> to inhale items on the ground near you. This
can come in handy when you <$cdef(27)>headbutt a tree to knock off its
berries, or when you break rocks and dirt with <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(4)>.

<$cdef(27)><$sklfull(13)> lets you move while you hover in the air. You can
float down or up by pressing <$keyicon(59)> or <$keyicon(58)> while using this move.

Select an item in your bag and press <$keyicon(0)> to spit it out. For certain
items, you can adjust the number of items you spit out at once by
pressing <$keyicon(30)> and redirect where you spit them out by using <$keyicon(31)>.
If you press <$keyicon(253)>, you can enter <$cdef(27)>replacement mode, which allows
you to swap what you want to spit out with what’s on the ground.

You can break what’s in front of you with <$keyicon(153)>. The broken item
will then be stored in your bag. If you press and hold the button
to break something, you will store it in your body so you can spit
it out whole.

You’ll get tired if you try to use moves while you’re out of <$cdef(27)>PP.
The gauge at the bottom right of the screen displays how much
<$cdef(27)>PP you have left.

You can restore your <$cdef(27)>PP by eating food, such as <$cdef(27)>berries and
vegetables. Open your bag with <$keyicon(159)> and select what you want
to eat with <$keyicon(0)>.

You can tell how much a Pokémon likes their home by checking
their <$cdef(27)>comfort level. Place things the Pokémon likes near their
home to raise their <$cdef(27)>comfort level.

Interested in raising a Pokémon’s <$cdef(27)>comfort level? Go ahead and
<$cdef(27)>ask them if they’re feeling comfy! They’ll let you know if there’s
anything they need from you. If you don’t have what they ask for,
check the <$cdef(27)>shop or go hunting for <$cdef(27)>recipes!

A Pokémon’s <$cdef(27)>comfort level will increase when they eat their
favorite food or if they eat until they are full.

You can give food directly to a Pokémon for them to eat, but you
can also put food on a <$cdef(27)>plate near their living space or plant a
<$cdef(27)>berry tree near their home. When the Pokémon is hungry, they
will eat on their own.

Place furniture around a Pokémon’s home for them to rest on,
such as a <$cdef(27)>bed or a <$cdef(27)>chair, to raise their <$cdef(27)>comfort level.

Pokémon can’t use <$cdef(27)>beds or <$cdef(27)>chairs that are smaller than they are.
Make sure to get big furniture for big Pokémon!

Place items around a Pokémon’s home that they can play
with, such as <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1274)> or <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1271)>, to raise their
<$cdef(27)>comfort level.

Different Pokémon like different things. Placing something a
Pokémon likes around their home will greatly raise their
<$cdef(27)>comfort level!

A Pokémon’s <$cdef(27)>comfort level also greatly increases when they
consume their favorite food or drink.
You can check your <$cdef(27)>Pokédex</color> to see what each Pokémon likes.

Pokémon also have different preferences when it comes to
<$cdef(27)>brightness, <$cdef(27)>temperature, and <$cdef(27)>humidity. Adjusting a Pokémon’s
home to match these preferences will raise that Pokémon’s
<$cdef(27)>comfort level.

You can check your <$cdef(27)>Pokédex to see a Pokémon’s <$cdef(27)>brightness,
<$cdef(27)>temperature, and <$cdef(27)>humidity preferences.

<$cdef(27)><$spwfull(1)>ing a house allows you to easily increase a Pokémon’s
<$cdef(27)>comfort level. Once construction on a house is finished, you can
invite Pokémon to move in.

The larger the house, the more the <$cdef(27)>comfort levels of the Pokémon
living there will increase.

The <$cdef(27)>comfort levels of Pokémon living in a house won’t be affected
by adjustments to brightness, temperature, or humidity outside
the house. Such adjustments need to be made <$cdef(27)>inside the house to
affect the <$cdef(27)>comfort levels of the Pokémon living there.

Roofs and light sources can affect the <$cdef(27)>brightness of a home. You
can brighten a home by placing lamps or streetlights around it.
Conversely, you can darken a home by placing a roof over it to
block light.

After you’ve used <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(2)> to make a crop field, you can
plant seeds and grow vegetables. Water your crops often, either
with <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(3)> or by other methods, to make sure they grow!

Press <$keyicon(153)> to harvest vegetables once they are ripe. You can then
water your vegetable plants with <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(3)> or other methods
to regrow them.

Each Pokémon has a <$cdef(27)>specialty. You can see a Pokémon’s specialty
in the <$cdef(27)>Pokédex, which you can access via the <$keyicon(4)> menu.

Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(10)> specialty will ignite nearby flammable
objects in their free time. If you’re traveling with a Pokémon who
has this specialty, just stand in front of what you want burned, and
they’ll set it ablaze for you.

Also, if you bring them to a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1446)>, they can melt
certain materials, such as metal or sand, for processing.

Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(1)> specialty will <$cdef(27)>lead other Pokémon
when building or remodeling structures. You can’t <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(1)>
anything without a leader Pokémon.

Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(5)> specialty will use their free time to
help nearby plants mature faster. If you bring a Pokémon with this
skill to a plant, they will help <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(5)> it for you!

Plants such as <$cdef(27)><$ifull(8)> won’t grow unless they’re watered,
even if a Pokémon who specializes in <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(5)>ing is with you.
Use <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(3)> or something similar to water your plants first,
then ask a Pokémon to help you grow them!

This parameter will <$cdef(27)>increase as you befriend more Pokémon and
raise their <$cdef(27)>comfort levels. As the <$cdef(27)>environment level goes up, you’ll
unlock more <$cdef(27)>challenges and <$cdef(27)>shop items!

Every Pokémon likes certain things—and every Pokémon dislikes
certain things too! If you place items that a Pokémon dislikes
around their home, their <$cdef(27)>comfort level will decrease.

Items that can heat or cool an area, such as <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1280)>
or <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1096)>, will change the <$cdef(27)>temperature of the home they’re
placed near.

Water, plants, and other related items will increase a home’s
<$cdef(27)>humidity. You can also remove those types of items from a home
to make it drier.

When you place an item for a Pokémon, be sure to place it near
their home. Items placed too far away will have no effect on the
Pokémon’s <$cdef(27)>comfort level.

You can press <$keyicon(32)> near a Pokémon’s home to display the area
around it. This area display will disappear if you press <$keyicon(32)> again
or if you move away from the home.

Legendary Pokémon have a greater effect on the <$cdef(27)>environment
level than other Pokémon, making it easier to <$cdef(27)>increase.

Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(6)> specialty can hold items for you.
Just tell one of these Pokémon “<$cdef(27)>I wanna check my storage” to add
items to or remove items from their inventory.

If you use a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(764)> while accompanied by a Pokémon who
is holding items for you, you can use any crafting materials they
are holding directly from their inventory.

When you travel with a Pokémon, they’ll help you out in various
ways. If you stand in front of something you need help with, the
Pokémon with you will use their specialty to try to help you out.

If you give <$cdef(27)><$ifull(3994)> to a Pokémon with the <$spwicon(26)><$cdef(27)>Gather Honey
specialty, they’ll give you furniture with special patterns in
exchange.

Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(15)> specialty will process <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1482)>
you give to them into <$cdef(27)><$ifull(407)>.

If you provide suitable materials to a Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(16)>
specialty, they will process those materials into other items.
You can travel with a Pokémon by <$cdef(27)>asking one to come with you</color>.

Press <$keyicon(214)> to invite all the Pokémon in front of you to follow you.
Up to five Pokémon can travel with you at a time.

When Pokémon are hungry, they may refuse to travel with you
or stop following you altogether. In those situations, give them
some food.

If you ask a<$cdef(27)> Pokémon “<$cdef(27)>How’s your comfort level?” they will tell
you how <$cdef(27)>comfortable they currently are. This will also allow you
to see how to raise that Pokémon’s <$cdef(27)>comfort level.

You can get information about an item or favor that the Pokémon
is requesting that day. Granting a Pokémon’s request will increase
their <$cdef(27)>comfort level.

Asking a Pokémon “<$cdef(27)>How’s your comfort level?” and granting their
request isn’t the only way to improve their <$cdef(27)>comfort. They may also
want other items or favors besides what they’ve requested. Feel
free to try different things when you have time!

Adding decorations to a Pokémon’s home, such as
<$cdef(27)><$ifull(1367)> or <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1542)>, will increase their
<$cdef(27)>comfort level.

If the <$cdef(27)>brightness of a Pokémon’s home matches their preference
or the hours of the day they are usually active, that Pokémon will
stay awake longer.

Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(8)> specialty will use nearby
<$cdef(27)><$ifull(1261)> you’ve filled to water surrounding plants.

Offer food at a <$cdef(27)><$hatname(152)> and bring a Pokémon with
the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(8)> specialty there to have them throw a <$cdef(27)>Rain Dance
party, which will increase the <$cdef(27)>humidity of the area.

Flower and tree seeds can be planted in the ground. Open your
bag, select the seeds to hold in your hands, and press <$keyicon(0)> to
plant them. Seeds can’t be planted in dry ground—be sure to wet
the ground with <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(3)> or something similar first!

It takes a little time for seeds to grow. Try waiting until the next
day to check on them.

When a Pokémon starts living in a habitat, that habitat becomes
their <$cdef(27)>home. Once a habitat becomes a home, no new Pokémon
will appear in that habitat. You will need to create more habitats
for new Pokémon to appear.

You can play <$cdef(27)>jump rope by talking to <$cdef(27)>Bulbasaur. Press <$keyicon(3)> at the
right time to jump over the vine—if it touches you, that’s the end
of the game!

This minigame can also be played with other players. When
playing with others, touching the vine removes you from the
game. The last player remaining wins the game. Rankings are
determined by the number of successful jumps each player made.

Players who’ve touched the vine can change its speed to hinder
players who are still jumping. Press <$keyicon(7)> to increase the vine’s
speed and <$keyicon(8)> to decrease it. The speed will change based on
how many players press the buttons, so work together as a team!

You can talk to <$cdef(27)>Zorua to play the <$cdef(27)>hide-and-sneak minigame.
To win, you must touch the <$cdef(27)>PC at the <$cdef(27)>Pokémon Center without
getting found by the seeker Pokémon. If you are found, you will
be sent back to the starting point.

Using <$cdef(27)><$sklfull(6)> will make it harder for the seeker Pokémon
to find you. You can also create distractions by placing items on
the ground, using items that make noise, or using emotes. Try
different types of diversions to create openings and keep moving
toward the <$cdef(27)>PC!

When you play hide-and-sneak with other players, it becomes a
team game. If any player touches the <$cdef(27)>PC, the whole team wins.
Players found by the seeker Pokémon will be sent back to the
starting point. Work with your team to reach the <$cdef(27)>PC!

If you talk to a Pokémon who has a problem that needs solving,
they may <$cdef(27)>request your help. You can check the <$cdef(27)>requests you’ve
accepted from the main menu at any time.

If you show a <$cdef(27)>lost relic to <$cdef(27)><$cname(341)>, who has the
<$cdef(27)><$spwfull(25)> specialty, they can tell you what kind of item
you’ve found.

<$cdef(27)>Drifloon can take you to mysterious places called <$cdef(27)>Dream Islands.
Some items can only be found on <$cdef(27)>Dream Islands, so explore them
thoroughly! When you’re ready to leave a <$cdef(27)>Dream Island, just talk
to <$cdef(27)>Drifloon.

You can only travel to <$cdef(27)>one Dream Island per day, but you can
revisit that island <$cdef(27)>as many times as you want. If you would like to
go to a different island, you’ll have to wait until the next day to
talk to <$cdef(27)>Drifloon again.

Enjoy your time here by chatting with other Pokémon, making all
sorts of items, or doing whatever you like at your own pace!

You can also look for new Pokémon, help the Pokémon you
already know with their <$cdef(27)>requests, or build your dream town—this
world is yours to enjoy as you see fit!

You can pick up things on the ground with <$keyicon(153)>. Anything you
pick up like this is automatically put in your bag.

You can use this move to <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(36)> into an object in front
of you. You can move around while transformed.

If you hold the <$cdef(27)><$ifull(2793)> and press <$keyicon(0)> while walking
with a Pokémon who has the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(11)> specialty, you’ll start
looking for buried items.

You can talk to a Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(27)> specialty to find out
<$cdef(27)>how humid it is currently.

You can set your handy bag to always display by opening your
bag and pressing <$keyicon(247)>. Items in your handy bag can be accessed
by pressing <$keyicon(161)> or <$keyicon(162)> without having to open your bag.

When there are multiple things nearby that you can interact with
(such as items to <$cdef(27)>pick up, objects to <$cdef(27)>inspect, or Pokémon to <$cdef(27)>talk
to), you can press <$keyicon(249)> to target a specific one. Give it a try if
you’re having trouble interacting with something!

Pokémon with the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(10)> specialty can process metals, such as
<$cdef(27)><$ifull(107)> and <$cdef(27)><$ifull(106)>, at a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1446)>.

If you encounter any mud while traveling with a Pokémon who
has the <$cdef(27)><$spwfull(8)> specialty, they’ll cover the mud with bubbles.
You can then spray the mud with water to wash it away!

Pokémon with the <$icon(10993)><$cdef(27)><$spwname(13)> specialty will pick up materials
and other items they find on the ground and place them in a
<$cdef(27)><$ifull(1460)>.

They can also bring materials from a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1460)> to
anywhere they can be processed, such as a <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1446)>.

A certain Pokémon will take you to a <$cdef(27)>Dream Island if you bring
them a <$cdef(27)>doll. Once you’ve visited a <$cdef(27)>Dream Island at least once,
you can get that Pokémon to come to you by interacting with
a <$cdef(27)>doll.

Pokémon with the <$icon(11222)><$cdef(27)><$spwname(30)> specialty can exchange <$cdef(27)>lost relics or
<$cdef(27)>rare feathers for other items.

You can give <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1801)> to Pokémon who have the
<$cdef(27)><$spwfull(17)> specialty to process into <$cdef(27)><$ifull(126)>!

<$cdef(27)><$cname(272)> has the <$icon(11219)><$cdef(27)><$spwname(28)> specialty and wants some food. Place
something to eat on an <$cdef(27)><$ifull(1811)>, and good things may
happen based on the food’s flavor or rarity!

<$cdef(27)><$cname(206)> has the <$icon(11008)><$cdef(27)><$spwname(21)> specialty and can use <$cdef(27)>bowls of paint
to change the color of many items, including furniture. However,
some items can’t be recolored.

They can also <$icon(11008)><$cdef(27)><$spwname(21)> patterns on items. If you find any <$cdef(27)>human
records that depict a pattern or items that have patterns on them,
bring them to <$cdef(27)><$cname(206)>.
